description: Elixir defines `if` as a macro over `case`. fz lowers `if` with no dispatch plan, so it is the one branch form the per-activation trim (fz-sc8.44) never reaches: `if true do a else b end` keeps both branches. Expected: `if` builds the same plan a two-arm boolean case builds, and its dead branch is trimmed like any other arm. Probe first: native has a fast path for plain conditions, so measure whether lowering an if as a case changes native code or the census, and state what the fast path is for before keeping or deleting it.
title: if is a case, as in Elixir
